name: Financial Markets
description: US equity and bond markets from 1926 to present. Track the growth of $10,000 across asset classes and see how market events intersect with personal financial milestones.

events.title: Stock Market Crash
events.description: The Dow Jones lost 89% of its value over 34 months. Starting in late October, the crash wiped out billions in investor wealth and triggered the Great Depression.

events.title: FDR Bank Holiday & New Deal
events.description: Emergency Banking Act closed and inspected all banks. The New Deal programs began stabilizing the financial system and restoring public confidence.

events.title: Post-WWII Economic Boom
events.description: Return of 12 million veterans and massive pent-up consumer demand ignited one of the longest sustained expansions in US history.

events.title: Dow Returns to 1929 Highs
events.description: The Dow Jones finally surpassed its 1929 peak after 25 years, confirming the full recovery from the Great Depression.

events.title: Great Society Inflation Begins
events.description: LBJ's Great Society spending combined with Vietnam War costs triggered persistent inflation, eroding real returns across asset classes.

events.title: Nixon Closes the Gold Window
events.description: Nixon ended the Bretton Woods system by suspending dollar convertibility to gold, permanently altering global currency dynamics.

events.title: Oil Crisis & Stagflation
events.description: OPEC oil embargo caused fuel prices to quadruple. Combined with high inflation and slow growth, stagflation devastated portfolios. S&P 500 lost ~48%.

events.title: Volcker Shock
events.description: Fed Chair Paul Volcker raised interest rates to 20% to break inflation. Caused a sharp recession but ultimately restored monetary credibility.

events.title: Great Bull Market Begins
events.description: Volcker's inflation victory triggered one of the longest bull markets in history. The S&P 500 would rise ~1400% over the next 18 years.

events.title: Black Monday
events.description: October 19, 1987: The Dow lost 22.6% in a single day — the largest single-day percentage drop in history. Markets recovered within two years.

events.title: Internet Boom
events.description: Netscape's IPO ignited the dot-com era. Venture capital flooded tech, and the S&P 500 returned 37.6% that year.

events.title: Dot-com Bust
events.description: The NASDAQ lost 78% from peak to trough. Trillions in market cap evaporated as technology valuations collapsed.

events.title: 9/11 Market Shock
events.description: Markets closed for four days following the September 11 attacks. The Dow fell 7.1% on reopening, the largest single-day point drop at the time.

events.title: Housing & Credit Boom
events.description: Low rates and financial innovation fueled a massive expansion in real estate and credit markets, setting the stage for the 2008 crisis.

events.title: Global Financial Crisis
events.description: Collapse of Lehman Brothers and the mortgage-backed securities market triggered the worst financial crisis since 1929. S&P 500 lost 37% in 2008 alone.

events.title: Federal Reserve Quantitative Easing
events.description: The Fed launched unprecedented QE programs, purchasing trillions in assets. This policy launched the longest bull market in US history (2009-2020).

events.title: Taper Tantrum
events.description: Fed's hint at reducing QE caused bond markets to sell off sharply. A preview of the volatility that follows policy normalization.

events.title: COVID-19 Market Crash
events.description: Fastest bear market in history — S&P 500 fell 34% in 33 days. Followed by the fastest recovery, aided by $5 trillion in fiscal stimulus.

events.title: Stimulus-Fueled Recovery
events.description: Trillions in government spending and ultra-low rates drove S&P 500 up 28.7%. Also sparked the highest inflation in 40 years.

events.title: Fed Rate Hike Cycle
events.description: Fed raised rates 11 times from 0.25% to 5.5% to combat 9% inflation. Bonds lost 26%, their worst year since 1788. S&P 500 fell 18%.

events.title: AI Bull Market
events.description: Generative AI enthusiasm drove S&P 500 up 26.3%. The Magnificent 7 tech stocks contributed over half of all index gains.
